subject: Re: PayGrid model fit eval - next steps & parity thresholds
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: model fit eval scope & parity thresholds

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the great conversation today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before we spin up the evals: 

Recap
- Goal: validate whether open models can meet PayGrid’s intent/QA bar for smart replies, routing, and 1–2 sentence follow-ups in the payments UX.
- Current proprietary baseline: PayGrid-prop-v1 (your on-prem model) — primary quality baseline for parity.
- Success criteria: functional parity on task-level metrics + acceptable regression on edge cases.

What Redwood will run (recommended initial matrix)
1) Redwood-rwd-13b-quant (Redwood curated open 13B, int8/4-bit profile) — target low-latency hosted option.
2) Open-Llama-13B-Chat (float16) — common open baseline.
3) Mistral-7B-Instruct (hf) — smaller, faster option for tail use-cases.

Acceptance thresholds (proposed)
- Intent accuracy: within ±3 percentage points of PayGrid-prop-v1 on your labeled dev set.
- F1/Task-level: no more than 5% absolute drop on fraud-detection/regression tasks you flagged.
- Safety/incorrect-action rate: <1% absolute increase vs baseline on the test set.

Attachments/Links I’m sending in this email
- paygrid_eval_prompt_set_v1.csv (sample prompt sets + preferred prompt templates) — attached.
- Drive folder with benchmarking rubric and our evaluation template: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cPayGridEval

Next steps
- If that matrix & thresholds look good to you, we’ll run a 7–10 day automated eval across your test set and provide an initial parity report.
- We’ll also provide a short canary rollout recommendation for the top candidate model (traffic % and rollback criteria).

Planned owners
- Redwood: Lauren (sales lead) + Marissa (solutions lead) + Aditya (ML engineering).
- PayGrid: Alex (product), procurement as needed for contracting.

Can you confirm scope & acceptance thresholds today so we can start Monday? Also send over the canonical test set (if it differs from the sample) and any additional negative examples we should include.

Thanks —

Lauren Bishop
Principal Solutions, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference

PS: attaching the prompt set (CSV) and a short stub of our benchmark rubric for your procurement team to review.
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@paygrid.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: PayGrid Procurement <procurement@paygrid.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model fit eval scope & parity thresholds

Thanks Lauren — this looks good. Quick responses: 

- Scope OK: matrix and thresholds look reasonable relative to what we discussed. The execs want a clear delta relative to PayGrid-prop-v1; the ±3% intent accuracy threshold should be fine as a starting point.
- Test set: attaching our canonical evaluation set (paygrid_test_set_v2.csv). It includes approx ~8k examples across intents, edge cases, and a flagged fraud-related subset.
- Timeline: procurement wants a short SOW for the eval (scope, data handling, timeline, and costs). Can you send that? We’re hoping to have an internal decision by 3/01, so a ~2-week turnaround on the first report would be ideal.

Questions for Redwood:
1) For the quantized profile (rwd-13b-quant), how do you handle KV-cache pinning and prefix caching for short-turn prompts? Any expected quality tradeoffs we should know?
2) Cost ballpark: can you provide an estimated cost range for the 7–10 day eval across the 3 model configs (not a formal quote — rough ballpark is fine).

If you can get the SOW + ballpark cost and an estimated start date, I’ll loop procurement and schedule the internal review.

— Alex
Product Lead, PayGrid
alex.chen@paygrid.com

On Sun, Feb 15, 2026 at 08:59 AM Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for your time today — attaching the prompt set and rubric as discussed.
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, PayGrid Procurement <procurement@paygrid.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model fit eval scope & parity thresholds

Alex —

Great, thanks for the test set. Attaching a short SOW draft and a benchmarking stub (open-models-benchmark-stub.pdf) in the Drive folder — link below. High-level answers to your questions: 

1) Quantized profile and prefix/KV cache behavior
- Our rwd-13b-quant profile uses a quantization-aware runtime that preserves KV-cache semantics. For short-turn prompts (typical of the PayGrid UX), we expect negligible latency impact and minimal quality delta vs float16 for the majority of intents. Edge cases (highly compositional prompts) can see small degradations — we’ll flag those specifically in the report.

2) Cost ballpark for eval (7–10 days across 3 configs)
- Approx range: $6k–$12k total depending on traffic replication and whether we run full-sweep sampling for temperature/grid tuning. We’ll provide a more precise breakdown in the SOW.

Planned deliverables
- Initial parity report (metrics vs PayGrid-prop-v1) with per-intent breakdowns and failure-case examples.
- Prompt-set adjustments and recommended guardrails.
- Canary rollout playbook for chosen candidate (traffic %, monitoring signals, rollback triggers).

Next steps (owners)
- Redwood: Marissa to run the eval job + produce the report; Aditya to handle model builds/quant profiles and early failure triage.
- PayGrid: Alex to share any additional negative examples and sign off on SOW.

If that all sounds good I’ll schedule a 30-minute kickoff this week to sync on test-set mapping and the data security controls in the SOW.

Link to SOW + rubric: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cPayGridEval

Thanks —

Lauren Bishop
Principal Solutions, Redwood Inference

Looping in here with a quick plan.

- Aditya: can you confirm the eval infra and quant profiles are ready to run against paygrid_test_set_v2.csv? I’ll kick off three parallel jobs (rwd-13b-quant, open-llama-13b-chat, mistral-7b-instruct) and collect per-intent metrics.
- I’ll build the parity dashboard (intent accuracy, F1, safety deltas) and include an examples tab with representative failure traces (for procurement visibility).
- If compute for rwd-13b-quant is an issue we can fall back to a smaller quantized candidate, but call that out in the SOW.

Estimated timing: 2–3 business days to get first-run metrics, full report in 7–10 days. I’ll add cost breakdowns to the SOW draft Lauren attached.
